claim.value: Each decisive midpoint result shrinks the candidate transition interval within the elimination procedure, conditional on valid endpoints, comparable trials and a persistent single transition.
claim.scope: Progress of the qualified revision-elimination procedure, not arbitrary midpoint testing.

provenance.rationale: The cited spans supply interval shrinkage, the elimination procedure and its explicit conditions.

signal_basis.value: Repeated representative exports yield a decisive midpoint classification from observed one-hour exceedance rates and their uncertainty, using prespecified classification and repeated-testing rules. The corresponding endpoint is replaced with that midpoint, discarding only history incompatible with the classification under the single-transition assumption.
signal_basis.scope: Decisive classifications within the qualified elimination procedure; inconclusive results do not authorize discarding history.

provenance.rationale: These spans describe repeated midpoint testing, measured tail-rate evidence, classification safeguards and the endpoint update that removes incompatible history.
This component is inapplicable because the claim is supported within its explicit conditions.

rationale: With valid endpoints, comparable trials and a persistent single transition, a decisive interior midpoint classification permits replacing the corresponding endpoint. That update narrows the candidate interval. This licenses the procedural progress claim without establishing sole causality or deployment safety.
uncertainty: Classification remains subject to the stated statistical evidence rules; the claim does not assert error-free localization.
